title: Evaluation of mandibular function following bilateral sagittal split osteotomy (BSSO)
summary:
Malocclusion can lead to difficulties in chewing, speaking, and breathing, as well as aesthetic impairments. In severe cases, surgical correction of the malocclusion is therefore necessary. Here, the jaw will be deliberately "broken", and fixed in a new position. 
In this study the range of motion of the lower jaw before and after surgery will be examined and compared. Additionally, the range of motion will be compared with an oral health-related quality of life questionnaire and a general questionnaire. 
The data collection will be conducted:
(1) before surgery,  as well as
(2) 4-8 weeks and  
(3) 9-12 months after surgery.
The following data will be collected: 
- general information about the patients (e.g., age, gender [...])
- information about the planned surgery (including virtual surgery planning) 
- any complications that may arise  
- range of motion of the lower jaw, and
- Questionnaires on oral health-related quality of life and subjective self-assessment.

interventions.name:
This monocentric observational study investigates 
(1) the range of mandibular motion as well as 
(2) quality of life and subjective self-evaluation
in patients with skeletal dysgnathia, both preoperatively and postoperatively.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Eligible for inclusion are patients capable of providing informed consent who present with skeletal dysgnathia and are scheduled to undergo a mandibular osteotomy as part of orthognathic surgery.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria are an acute trauma in the jaw region, a history of temporomandibular joint trauma, or previous orthognathic surgery involving the mandible.
